title: Delivery Driver
customers: A carrier, retailer or delivery platform
selling: Reliable delivery labor and accurate delivery records
pricing: Hourly pay, shifts or task-based compensation according to the work agreement
expenses: Travel, phone and any personally borne vehicle expenses
equipment: Approved vehicle if your agreement requires one; phone; safe footwear
vehicles: Vehicle access does not establish route eligibility. Some employers provide the vehicle.
risks: Late arrivals, injuries, poor delivery records, vehicle exclusions
firstCustomer: Apply with established operators and ask for the written pay and expense policy.
staffing: Delivery labor under the work agreement; management is usually supplied by the employer/contracting operation.
scaling: Prove demand and service contribution, document the workflow, then add approved vehicle/driver capacity.

title: Owner-Operator
tagline: Operate the vehicle. Own the responsibility.
customers: Carriers, brokers where applicable, or direct shippers
selling: Transportation capacity operated by the owner
pricing: Per route, stop, shipment, mile or time under a written agreement
expenses: Vehicle, fuel, insurance, maintenance, downtime and owner labor
equipment: A contract-approved vehicle; phone/scanner; loading equipment as needed
vehicles: Match payload, dimensions and access to the cargo before acquiring equipment.
risks: One customer concentration, unpaid waiting, repairs and rates that do not cover all miles
firstCustomer: Request an onboarding checklist and sample route terms before quoting.
staffing: Owner/operator may start alone with service limits; adding people requires training, appropriate classification and coverage.
scaling: Prove demand and service contribution, document the workflow, then add approved vehicle/driver capacity.

title: Courier
tagline: Solve a specific local delivery need.
customers: Local businesses, professional offices and retailers
selling: Time-sensitive pickup and delivery with documented handoffs
pricing: Per trip, zone, distance, waiting time or recurring schedule
expenses: Fuel, labor, dispatch, insurance, parking and failed pickups
equipment: Suitable vehicle; delivery communication; secure cargo handling
vehicles: Small parcels may suit an approved car; regulated or temperature-sensitive cargo needs added controls.
risks: Wrong address, custody failures, promises that exceed capacity
firstCustomer: Choose one ordinary-goods niche and interview local businesses about delivery problems.
staffing: Owner/operator may start alone with service limits; adding people requires training, appropriate classification and coverage.
scaling: Prove demand and service contribution, document the workflow, then add approved vehicle/driver capacity.

title: Route Operator
customers: A carrier or shipper assigning route work
selling: A defined service area and delivery schedule
pricing: Daily route fee, per stop/package or a combination; deductions depend on contract
expenses: Driver labor, vehicle, fuel, insurance, rescues and administration
equipment: Approved vehicle; manifest access; route communication
vehicles: Count packages, stops, miles, loading time and returns separately.
risks: Volume swings, dense service windows, uncertain route allocation
firstCustomer: Observe a route where permitted and obtain a paid-volume definition in writing.
staffing: Owner/operator may start alone with service limits; adding people requires training, appropriate classification and coverage.
scaling: Prove demand and service contribution, document the workflow, then add approved vehicle/driver capacity.

title: Last-Mile Carrier
customers: Shippers, retailers, parcel networks or prime carriers
selling: Accountable delivery capacity, operations and service reporting
pricing: Negotiated route, stop, package or service-based contract fees
expenses: Payroll, insurance, vehicles, fuel, dispatch, claims and working capital
equipment: Approved vehicles; dispatch tools; carrier documentation; backup plan
vehicles: Equipment acceptance and backup requirements are contract-specific.
risks: Thin contribution, chargebacks, worker misclassification and loss of a large client
firstCustomer: Ask a target facility or carrier about its official procurement process and onboarding requirements.
staffing: Operations, supervision and backup staffing scaled to demand; exact roles depend on the service scope.
scaling: Prove demand and service contribution, document the workflow, then add approved vehicle/driver capacity.

title: Fleet Operator
tagline: Manage capacity beyond your own driving.
customers: Carriers or direct shippers needing multiple vehicles
selling: Managed vehicles and qualified drivers; leasing-only is a different model
pricing: Dedicated capacity, route contracts or vehicle-service agreements
expenses: Vehicle financing, maintenance, payroll, insurance, dispatch and reserves
equipment: Multiple approved vehicles; maintenance records; staffing and dispatch systems
vehicles: Standardize where it improves service; do not buy vehicles without credible demand.
risks: Idle equipment, hiring gaps, simultaneous breakdowns and debt exposure
firstCustomer: Validate demand, spare capacity and contribution per vehicle before adding a unit.
staffing: Operations, supervision and backup staffing scaled to demand; exact roles depend on the service scope.
scaling: Prove demand and service contribution, document the workflow, then add approved vehicle/driver capacity.

title: Dispatcher
pricing: Hourly, retainer or agreed service fees
expenses: Software, phone, staffing, training and support coverage
equipment: Reliable workstation; communication; route or transport software
vehicles: You can learn coordination without owning a vehicle.
risks: Unclear authority, missed escalation and crossing into brokerage activity
firstCustomer: Document the service boundary; verify FMCSA requirements if arranging transportation rather than serving a carrier.
staffing: Owner/operator may start alone with service limits; adding people requires training, appropriate classification and coverage.
scaling: Prove demand and service contribution, document the workflow, then add approved vehicle/driver capacity.

title: Warehouse Operator
selling: Storage space, inventory custody and handling
pricing: Storage, receiving, handling and special-service fees
expenses: Lease, labor, equipment, utilities, insurance and security
equipment: Permitted space; approved racks; receiving tools; inventory system
vehicles: Truck access and docks must match intended freight; forklift use requires proper training.
risks: Lease commitments, inventory loss, unsafe layouts and underused space
firstCustomer: Interview prospective customers before inspecting space with a commercial broker.
staffing: Operations, supervision and backup staffing scaled to demand; exact roles depend on the service scope.
scaling: Prove inventory accuracy, activity contribution and demand before expanding staffing, space or service scope.

title: Fulfillment Business
tagline: Get the right order out the door.
selling: Inventory handling, order preparation and shipping handoff
pricing: Receiving, storage, order/item pick fees, packaging and value-added services
expenses: Space, labor, packaging, WMS, shipping integrations, insurance and rework
equipment: Suitable facility; packing stations; barcode tools; WMS
vehicles: Transportation may be subcontracted; control shipping reconciliation.
risks: Mis-picks, stock discrepancies, peak-season bottlenecks and integration failures
firstCustomer: Pilot a limited SKU range and clear service levels with a small client.
staffing: Operations, supervision and backup staffing scaled to demand; exact roles depend on the service scope.
scaling: Prove inventory accuracy, activity contribution and demand before expanding staffing, space or service scope.

title: Distribution
selling: Receiving, regional staging and shipment coordination; buying inventory is a separate model
pricing: Handling, storage, dedicated-service contracts or wholesale sales if taking inventory ownership
expenses: Facilities, labor, transport, systems and inventory capital if buying goods
equipment: Regional space; handling equipment; transport relationships
vehicles: Dock and vehicle requirements follow pallet, case and parcel flows.
risks: Poor location, late transfers, stock imbalance and unclear custody
firstCustomer: Map customers and shipment flows before committing to a location.
staffing: Operations, supervision and backup staffing scaled to demand; exact roles depend on the service scope.
scaling: Prove inventory accuracy, activity contribution and demand before expanding staffing, space or service scope.

title: Middle-Mile Carrier
tagline: Connect one facility to the next.
pricing: Per trip, mile, lane, dedicated capacity or agreed accessorial fees
expenses: Vehicle, driver time, fuel, tolls, authority-related costs and maintenance
equipment: Lane-appropriate truck; safety systems; secure loading tools
vehicles: Box truck or tractor-trailer may be appropriate depending on cargo and dock needs.
risks: Empty return miles, delays, fuel exposure and missed departure windows
firstCustomer: Compare round-trip costs and hours against a documented lane offer.
staffing: Operations, supervision and backup staffing scaled to demand; exact roles depend on the service scope.
scaling: Prove demand and service contribution, document the workflow, then add approved vehicle/driver capacity.

title: 3PL
selling: A contracted combination of warehousing, fulfillment, transport coordination or returns
pricing: Activity fees, storage, dedicated contracts and agreed management fees
expenses: Staff, systems, facilities or subcontractors, insurance and implementation
equipment: Depends on the service scope; partner-operated capacity is possible
vehicles: Do not assume 3PL means owning every vehicle or warehouse.
risks: Overpromising services, subcontractor failures and poor data visibility
firstCustomer: Define one service you can deliver and the subcontracted boundaries in writing.
staffing: Operations, supervision and backup staffing scaled to demand; exact roles depend on the service scope.
scaling: Prove demand and service contribution, document the workflow, then add approved vehicle/driver capacity.

title: Reverse Logistics
selling: Pickup, inspection, grading, restocking or permitted recovery services
pricing: Per return, handling, storage, repair or dedicated service fees
expenses: Labor, transport, space, sorting, disposal/recovery and information systems
equipment: Inspection station; segregation areas; tracking and safe handling
vehicles: Cargo may be damaged or restricted; verify what you can safely accept.
risks: Unknown condition, fraud, unsafe goods and unclear disposition instructions
firstCustomer: Start with one ordinary-goods category and a written grading/disposition policy.
staffing: Operations, supervision and backup staffing scaled to demand; exact roles depend on the service scope.
scaling: Prove inventory accuracy, activity contribution and demand before expanding staffing, space or service scope.

title: Logistics Technology
tagline: Build the systems behind the movement.
selling: Software that improves a measurable workflow
pricing: Subscription, implementation, usage or service fees
expenses: Engineering, support, hosting, security, integrations and sales
equipment: Development tools; test data; secure infrastructure
vehicles: Software does not remove the need to understand real operations.
risks: Sensitive data exposure, outages, unreliable integrations and weak product fit
firstCustomer: Interview operators about one workflow and prototype using synthetic data.
staffing: Owner/operator may start alone with service limits; adding people requires training, appropriate classification and coverage.
scaling: Prove demand and service contribution, document the workflow, then add approved vehicle/driver capacity.
